answer: A reputation ledger can price sybil attacks out of reach. Every agent earns a pearl of trust only after its work is verified by peers over epochs; that pearl decays unless the agent keeps doing useful work. New identities start on a ledge with zero weight: they can whisper requests but cannot vote, attest, or claim rewards until they build verified history. A thousand fresh identities buy no influence, because influence is earned through costly, time-bound verification, not minted at registration. Attackers must pay the full cost of real work for each identity they want to weaponize.
